questions.q: 0.50 g of magnesium (0.0208 mol) reacts with excess copper(II) sulfate solution (50 cm³). The temperature rises from 21.0 °C to 46.0 °C. (a) Calculate Q [2]. (b) Calculate ΔH in kJ/mol [3]. (c) Give two reasons the value is less exothermic than the data-book value [2]. (d) State the sign of ΔH and why [1].
questions.a: (a) Q = 50 × 4.2 × 25 = 5250 J (2); (b) 5.25 kJ ÷ 0.0208 (1) = 252 (1); ΔH = -252 kJ/mol (1); (c) heat lost to surroundings; not all Mg reacted or heat absorbed by the cup (2); (d) negative: exothermic, temperature rose (1)

questions.q: Explain why heating blue copper(II) sulfate is endothermic but adding water to the white solid is exothermic.
questions.a: Reversible reaction (1); same energy transferred in each direction (1); in opposite directions: taken in when heated, given out when water added (1)
